title: Judge orders ethics probe into Trump’s Washington golf course project
full_text:
Investing.com -- A federal judge has appointed a former top prosecutor to investigate possible ethical misconduct by Trump administration lawyers defending President Donald Trump’s plans to renovate a historic public golf course in Washington.
U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes named Jessie Liu, a former U.S. attorney for the District of Columbia, as special master on Friday to examine the conduct of Justice Department and Interior Department attorneys in litigation over East Potomac Golf Links.
The appointment follows an October 30 hearing at which Reyes ordered an ethics investigation, questioning whether government lawyers had misrepresented the administration’s intentions to proceed with renovations despite a temporary court order blocking the project.
Trump had said construction would begin immediately, contradicting assurances government officials had given the court, according to the judge. Reyes also challenged attorneys’ attempts to persuade her to discount the president’s public statements about the project.
The inquiry adds a separate dispute over the government’s representations to the court to a lawsuit initially focused on the legality of redeveloping the publicly accessible course.
Liu served as Washington’s chief federal prosecutor during Trump’s first administration and oversaw the criminal prosecution of Roger Stone, a longtime Trump associate. She later worked in private practice before establishing a law firm with two other former prosecutors in April.
The Interior Department criticized Reyes following the appointment, accusing her of political bias and opposing the president’s efforts to improve the capital.
Trump wants to turn the East Potomac course into a high-end golf destination as part of a broader effort to reshape prominent public spaces in Washington.
The underlying lawsuit was brought by a nonprofit organization and two Washington residents. They argue that the proposed reconstruction of East Potomac Park, including the golf course, violates environmental requirements and a congressional preservation law.
The special master’s assignment concerns the conduct of government lawyers, rather than a final determination on whether the renovation itself can proceed.

title: Nvidia-backed Groq seeks $8 billion valuation in new funding round - Bloomberg
full_text:
Investing.com -- Nvidia-backed artificial intelligence infrastructure company Groq is seeking fresh funding at an $8 billion valuation, more than doubling its valuation in three months despite a selloff in publicly traded data center operators, Bloomberg reported exclusively, citing investor documents.
Executive Chairman Alex Davis has approached investors about a new Series B financing round at the proposed valuation, excluding the capital raised.
The fundraising follows an August round that valued Groq at $3.15 billion before a $350 million investment, marking a sharp increase in its ambitions as investors question the sustainability of AI infrastructure spending.
Shares of neocloud operators CoreWeave and Nebius have faced selling pressure amid concerns over heavy borrowing and potential regulatory resistance to data center development following the U.S. midterm elections.
In a letter to investors, Davis argued that Groq’s business model offers an advantage over competitors relying heavily on debt financing.
He said the company could generate growing profit margins without taking on substantial leverage, criticizing rival operators for accumulating financial obligations that could undermine their businesses.
Groq previously developed specialized AI chips to compete with Nvidia before shifting its focus toward operating data centers providing computing capacity for AI inference.
The transition followed a $20 billion licensing agreement with Nvidia late last year, under which the chipmaker recruited Groq founder and former Chief Executive Jonathan Ross alongside other employees.
The remaining business now concentrates on supplying inference computing services, particularly for cybersecurity applications.
The proposed financing would support growing demand through short- and medium-term customer contracts, according to the investor letter.
Davis expects revenue to increase eightfold next year, with earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization reaching $2 billion by 2028.
The fundraising effort comes as competition intensifies among AI infrastructure providers and investors scrutinize the profitability of large-scale computing investments.
Groq and Davis’s investment firm, Disruptive, declined to comment on the fundraising plans.

title: Goldman raises global data center capacity forecast to 273 GW by 2030
full_text:
Investing.com -- Goldman Sachs raised its forecast for global data center capacity to 273 gigawatts by 2030 from 217 gigawatts previously, citing stronger artificial intelligence infrastructure demand and expectations for further project announcements.
The revised outlook implies 170 GW of additional capacity from 2025, when worldwide supply stood at approximately 103 GW, according to a November 2 research note.
The expansion could require $8.5 trillion in cumulative capital expenditure over five years, based on an estimated $50 billion per gigawatt, including computing infrastructure.
Annual global capacity additions are projected to reach 25 GW in 2026, 32 GW in 2027 and 35 GW in 2028. Longer-term forecasts were increased to account for projects not yet announced.
The U.S. capacity estimate rose to 152 GW by 2030 from 125 GW previously, representing 103 GW of new capacity after 2025. The country is expected to account for roughly 60% to 70% of worldwide additions through 2030.
Expanding cloud, neocloud and related facilities supporting demand for graphics processing units contributed to the U.S. revision. Those categories added 11.8 GW to cumulative capacity forecasts for 2026 through 2030.
Large high-performance computing facilities associated with AI workloads are expected to dominate construction. Projects of at least 75 megawatts could represent 66% of global additions and 75% of U.S. additions by 2028.
Consensus projections for selected U.S. technology and cloud companies indicate annual capital expenditure could reach approximately $1.74 trillion by 2030, compared with $457 billion in 2025.
The outlook also identifies mounting construction risks, including limited power availability, permitting delays, community opposition and rising financing costs. High-performance computing developments typically rely on debt financing covering 80% to 90% of project costs.
Projects with secured electricity supplies and clear regulatory approvals are seen as better positioned to proceed, particularly as developers confront tighter financing conditions and heightened scrutiny of new facilities.

title: ’Special master’ named for ethics probe in lawsuit over Trump’s DC golf project
full_text:
By Steve Gorman and Richard Cowan
WASHINGTON, Nov 7 (Reuters) - A judge said on Saturday she would appoint a former top federal prosecutor to investigate whether Trump administration lawyers committed ethical violations in their defense of President Donald Trump’s plans to close and renovate a historic public golf course in Washington.
US District Judge Ana Reyes named Jessie Liu, former US attorney for the District of Columbia, as a "special master" to investigate the conduct of the departments of Justice and Interior during litigation over the fate of the East Potomac Golf Links course.
Reyes named Liu one week after an October 30 hearing in which the judge ordered an ethics probe and expressed concerns that government attorneys misrepresented the Trump administration’s intention to continue with the renovation of the East Potomac course despite her temporary order blocking the project.
At that time, Trump had said renovation work would begin immediately, despite the judge’s order and contrary to assertions that Reyes said government officials had made asking her to disregard the president’s statements.
"Rarely, if ever, has the United States Department of Justice urged a federal court not to believe the sitting president," Reyes said at an earlier hearing. "This started as a case about golf ... But it has become much more."
Liu was the US attorney for DC during Trump’s first term, when she oversaw the criminal case against Trump’s longtime friend and adviser Roger Stone. After a few years in private practice, Liu and two other former prosecutors launched their own law firm in April.
The Interior Department issued a statement calling Reyes a "far Left activist judge" who would "stop at nothing to prevent President Donald Trump’s efforts to beautify our nation’s capital."
Trump’s plan to transform the East Potomac links into a "world class" golf course is part of a broader effort to leave his architectural stamp on Washington.
The lawsuit filed by a non-profit group and two Washington residents asserts that the planned reconstruction of East Potomac Park, including the golf course, violates environmental laws and a congressional preservation act.
(Writing and reporting by Steve Gorman in Los Angeles; Additional reporting by Richard Cowan in Washington; Editing by Sergio Non and Sonali Paul)

title: New Zealand election puts tax reform party in kingmaker role as majority hangs
full_text:
Investing.com -- New Zealand’s election has left Prime Minister Christopher Luxon facing a fragile path to another term, with a newcomer proposing sweeping tax changes potentially holding the balance of power once outstanding ballots are counted.
The governing alliance of National, ACT and New Zealand First secured a provisional 67 seats in the expanded 131-member parliament, just enough for a majority. National won 42 seats, ACT 13 and New Zealand First 12.
But nearly 400,000 special votes, representing about 14% of ballots, remain uncounted until November 27. These votes have historically favored left-leaning parties and could erase the coalition’s narrow advantage.
That uncertainty has brought Qiulae Wong, the 38-year-old leader of the centrist Opportunity Party, into focus. Her party won a projected seven seats with 5.96% of the vote, potentially positioning it to negotiate support for the next government.
Opportunity proposes an annual NZ19,400(10,800) universal basic income for most residents, funded by a 1.75% annual land tax. Both major parties have rejected the proposals, creating an obstacle to any agreement.
Luxon previously ruled out governing with Opportunity but indicated Sunday that building a relationship with Wong would be appropriate. Labour leader Chris Hipkins is also waiting for final results before coalition negotiations.
The center-left Labour, Greens and Te Pāti Māori bloc is projected to hold 57 seats, rising to 64 with Opportunity, still short of the 66 seats needed for a majority in the projected parliament.
The election also exposed declining support for established parties. National and Labour each received just over 29% of votes, as smaller parties gained ground amid voter frustration over living costs.
The incumbent coalition remains in office in a caretaker capacity, limiting major decisions until a government is formed. Parliament must convene by January 14, and Hipkins has expressed hopes of reaching an agreement before Christmas.

title: U.S. military disables cargo vessel attempting to breach Iran blockade
full_text:
Investing.com -- U.S. forces disabled a commercial cargo vessel in the Gulf of Oman on Saturday after it attempted to breach Washington’s naval blockade of Iran, marking a fresh escalation in efforts to restrict Tehran’s maritime trade.
The St. Kitts-flagged ship had visited an Iranian port and was attempting to leave regional waters when an American military aircraft fired precision munitions at its stern, according to U.S. Central Command.
The military said personnel directed the vessel’s crew to leave the sections targeted before the strike. It did not provide details about casualties, damage beyond the disabled ship, or the vessel’s cargo.
The incident comes amid a months-long U.S. blockade intended to curb Iran’s exports and restrict access to materials that could support its military activities.
Central Command estimates the maritime restrictions have prevented Iran from exporting more than $25 billion worth of crude oil, highlighting the economic pressure Washington says it has imposed on Tehran.
In a separate announcement Saturday, the U.S. military said it was establishing a task force to disrupt Iranian shipments of advanced weapons and other sanctioned materials across land borders and through the Caspian Sea.
The expanded operation suggests Washington is seeking to close routes beyond the Gulf and surrounding shipping lanes, adding another layer of enforcement to its existing naval measures.
The developments come amid renewed threats of military action from President Donald Trump, who has warned that the United States could launch another offensive against Iran.
Tehran has responded with warnings of widespread retaliation against infrastructure across the Gulf, raising concerns about the security of regional facilities and commercial activity.
The confrontation also places renewed attention on energy shipments through waters near Iran, where restrictions on maritime traffic can complicate regional trade.
Central Command did not say whether the disabled vessel would be detained, allowed to proceed after repairs, or subjected to further enforcement action.

title: AI stock selloff drives investors to China, India, and overlooked Asian sectors
full_text:
Investing.com -- Investors are shifting toward Chinese and Indian equities and less technology-dependent Asian sectors as a selloff in artificial intelligence stocks raises concerns about valuations and returns on massive infrastructure spending.
The rotation follows a sharp decline in semiconductor-heavy markets after the U.S. midterm elections, with investors reassessing their exposure to companies supplying the global AI expansion.
South Korea’s Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, alongside Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, have faced selling pressure as doubts grow over whether AI investment will deliver sufficient profits.
China has emerged as a potential alternative. A Hong Kong index tracking mainland Chinese companies gained 5.2% last week, its strongest performance since March 2025, as investors sought cheaper valuations and less concentrated technology exposure.
India attracted even stronger buying. The Nifty 50 surged 8.6%, its biggest weekly advance since 2021, supported by renewed foreign interest and expectations that easing oil prices could benefit the energy-importing economy.
Overseas investors purchased a net $1.9 billion of Indian equities through Wednesday, reversing earlier weakness in a market that had lagged global peers for much of the year.
Investment managers are increasingly favoring domestic growth opportunities, including Indian financial companies, contract drug manufacturers and consumer-focused businesses. Vietnam is also attracting attention for its domestic growth prospects.
In South Korea, investors are looking beyond major chipmakers toward cosmetics, entertainment, retail and food companies, whose revenues are less directly tied to AI infrastructure spending.
Elsewhere, healthcare and consumer staples are gaining attention, alongside manufacturers that could benefit from reduced U.S. trade barriers.
LG Electronics has emerged as one potential beneficiary of easing tariff pressures, given its exposure to American household appliance and television markets. Japanese and Korean automakers are also drawing renewed interest.
Some investors still view the AI downturn as a buying opportunity, but the immediate shift favors diversification into businesses with different earnings drivers.

title: 5 big analyst AI moves: Is the historic AI stock rout a buy opportunity?
full_text:
Investing.com -- Here are the biggest analyst moves in the area of artificial intelligence (AI) for this week.
AI rout is a buying opportunity, Yardeni says
Yardeni Research told investors the selloff in Thursday’s session represents a buying opportunity, arguing that political backlash against data centers is a speed bump for the AI boom rather than a roadblock.
"Since September 15, we’ve counseled proceeding with caution in the stock market through the midterm elections," the firm wrote, adding that it had anticipated buying opportunities after Tuesday’s elections. Stocks rallied Wednesday, driven by short covering, but then plunged, with the S&P 500’s 4.4% decline its worst day since the April 2025 tariff shock and the Nasdaq’s 5.5% drop pushing it into correction territory.
"The cold shower we warned might follow a democratic sweep arrived late," Yardeni said.
On Thursday, investors began "discounting the implications of the Democratic sweep for the economy’s golden goose: the AI investment boom." Yardeni pointed to growing backlash against data centers, citing an NBC exit poll showing 76% of voters opposed new facilities in their communities.
"Perhaps most consequentially, Texas, which accounts for nearly 30% of planned US data center additions in 2028, elected Gina Hinojosa as governor after she promised to halt new approvals," Yardeni said. Goldman Sachs estimates that states facing possible restrictions account for around 45% of planned U.S. data center capacity.
Still, Yardeni believes the backlash, alongside financial and physical bottlenecks, are "just speed bumps" and that the selling is overdone. "Data centers will get built, albeit at a slower pace. Speed bumps should prevent the AI boom from moving too fast and crashing around the next curve," it said.
"That’s why we view Thursday’s sell off as a buying opportunity."
Analysts downgrade Marvell on concerns over all-stock deal with Lumentum
Earlier this week, TD Cowen and Bank of America have both downgraded Marvell Technology, citing concerns about the chipmaker’s all-stock acquisition of Lumentum.
TD Cowen cut Marvell to Hold from Buy, slashing its price target to $175 from $350. Analyst Sean O’Loughlin expects the deal to dilute EPS by a mid-single-digit percentage in 2028, its first year, and worries it may come at or near the peak of an optical mini-cycle.
"Our downgrade is driven primarily by our negative view of the transaction itself in terms of structure and timing, rather than the quality of the asset Marvell is acquiring," he wrote.
O’Loughlin said Lumentum is likely to become a "crown jewel" within Marvell’s portfolio, but noted that bottom-up consensus implies a roughly $100 billion optical transceiver market in 2027, compared with TD Cowen’s $47 billion forecast. If the cycle turns, Lumentum’s operating leverage could worsen the dilution.
Bank of America downgraded Marvell to Neutral from Buy and cut its price target to $225 from $400. Analyst Vivek Arya cited a potential extended stock overhang from the deal, along with a big drop in the SOX index over the past month.
Arya said the deal has strategic merit, creating a broader electrical-to-optical connectivity platform, but flagged a lengthy regulatory process with closing expected in the first half of 2028, limited EPS accretion as $1 billion in cost cuts falls short of offsetting about 50% share dilution, and potential customer conflicts.
"There was no mention of any large M&A in MRVL’s recent analyst day, so the news comes as a considerable surprise," he said. "We question the impact on LITE’s valuation once its laser shortages are inevitably resolved."
Citi says AI trade may stay under pressure post-midterms, prefers Europe over U.S. stocks
Citi told clients the AI trade could remain under pressure after the U.S. midterm elections, and said it prefers European stocks over U.S. equities for now.
The bank noted that markets typically pull back ahead of midterms and rally afterward, with seasonal analysis pointing to November-December S&P 500 returns of 3% to 4%. But this year’s pre-election weakness had other causes.
"More importantly, the pullback ahead of the midterms was not mostly due to the election, but due to AI financing worries, and oil," the bank wrote.
Citi still expects data centers to get built given strong demand for computing power, but said their location, design and pace of construction may change after Democrats’ gains. "This is far from ideal for the picks and shovels, including semis," the bank said.
Its "Generals" index, which tracks how many of the seven largest S&P 500 stocks trade below their 200-day moving averages, is close to triggering a cautionary signal, and Citi expects more rotation out of tech for now.
Citi said the election has not clearly changed the Iran war’s trajectory, but a renewed escalation does not appear imminent, with a third U.S. aircraft carrier not due in the Gulf until mid- to late November.
"We prefer to use Europe, given that the AI story remains difficult, while the large move lower in oil should benefit European equities much more, also because it may lead to a more dovish ECB," Citi said. At the very least, it expects European stocks to outperform the U.S.
Citi cuts Adobe to Sell, sees "rising risk of a hard reset"
In a separate note, Citi has downgraded Adobe to Sell and slashed its price target to $207 from $250, saying it sees downside risk to consensus growth estimates into fiscal 2027 as a leadership transition coincides with mounting competitive and macro pressure on the Creative business.
"[We] see rising risk of a hard reset," Citi analysts said. Incoming CEO Anil Chakravarthy, who takes over Dec. 1, assumes the role "amid key leadership vacancies," including the CFO and the head of Digital Media.
The Wall Street firm expects a weaker fiscal 2027 outlook when Adobe reports fourth-quarter results in early December. "A ’hard reset’ would pressure shares near term but provide time to rebuild leadership, refine strategy, and establish a more achievable base to accelerate," the analysts wrote.
The bank expects Adobe to lean more on top-of-funnel growth through AI and Firefly rather than its classic Creative Cloud suite, which has relied on price increases. That shift toward monthly active users will likely weigh on total ARR in fiscal 2027 and 2028, with the greatest impact in core Creative, compounded by weak small-business demand and competition from web-based and AI-native tools.
Citi estimates the user-growth emphasis could add 200 basis points of pressure to fiscal 2027 annual recurring revenue (ARR) growth, with pricing facing a further 50 basis point headwind as Adobe laps earlier Creative Cloud increases.
It cut net new ARR estimates for fiscal 2027 and 2028 by roughly $470 million and $500 million, to $1.5 billion and $1.35 billion, taking total ARR growth to 5.3% and 4.5% year-over-year, 200 to 300 basis points below Street estimates.
Citi also lowered its fiscal 2027 non-GAAP gross margin estimate by 70 basis points to reflect unmonetized AI inference costs, and sees sharply lower revenue in fiscal 2028 alongside modest margin degradation.
Wall Street analysts downgrade HubSpot on weak Q4 outlook
Four Wall Street firms have downgraded HubSpot after the software company’s weaker-than-expected fourth-quarter outlook pointed to a worsening demand environment.
HubSpot’s third-quarter revenue grew 17% at constant currency, a 2-point beat, but it guided fourth-quarter growth to 12%, below consensus of 13.8%. Management said budget scrutiny, price sensitivity and longer sales cycles had become more pronounced and are likely to persist into 2027.
The company added 5,300 net new customers in the quarter, below the 5,600 expected, and now expects fewer than 5,000 in the fourth quarter, while net revenue retention slipped to 101% from 103% a year ago.
BTIG cut HubSpot to Neutral from Buy and lowered its 2027 growth forecast to 11% from 14%. Analyst Nick Altmann said the stock looks appropriately valued at about 10 times 2027 estimated free cash flow.
KeyBanc downgraded the stock to Sector Weight. "We recognize this is late, but we believe there is little room for improvement between now and when we get formal 2027 guidance next February and are downgrading to Sector Weight," analyst Jackson Ader wrote.
Cantor downgraded HubSpot to Underweight with a $170 price target. Analyst Matthew VanVliet said the company’s new European pricing effectively amounts to a price cut and that its AI tools are underperforming peers.
"We no longer see HUBS as a premier SaaS asset that deserves the benefit of the doubt," he said.
Separately, Morgan Stanley also cut HubSpot to Equal-weight from Overweight and trimmed its price target to $229 from $287.

title: Saudi Arabia lifts oil region alerts after Houthi missile intercepted
full_text:
Investing.com -- Saudi Arabia lifted emergency alerts across parts of its oil-producing Eastern Province on Sunday, shortly before a Saudi-led military coalition announced it had intercepted a ballistic missile fired toward the region by Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi movement.
The civil defence authority issued an all-clear for Dhahran, Dammam, Abqaiq and Al-Ahsa after initially warning residents of potential danger. Officials did not specify the nature of the earlier threat or report damage from the latest incident.
Dhahran hosts the headquarters of state-owned Saudi Aramco, placing the alert close to one of the world’s most important oil companies. The headquarters sustained extensive damage in an attack in October, adding to concerns about the security of the kingdom’s energy infrastructure.
Abqaiq is another significant location within the province, which holds most of Saudi Arabia’s oil and gas reserves. Threats to the area can attract attention from energy traders concerned about disruptions to crude production, processing and exports.
The coalition fighting in Yemen said it intercepted a ballistic missile launched by the Houthis toward Saudi Arabia’s Eastern region. Its announcement followed the lifting of the civil defence warnings, although authorities did not explicitly connect the earlier alerts to the intercepted missile.
The Houthis have repeatedly targeted Saudi airports, ports and oil facilities with missiles and drones, increasing security pressures on the kingdom as fighting across the Middle East continues.
The wider conflict began in February with U.S. and Israeli attacks on Iran. Saudi Arabia, a U.S. ally, has faced attacks by the Iran-aligned Yemeni group amid the regional confrontation.
Sunday’s alerts were brief, and the authorities’ subsequent all-clear indicated that immediate warnings had ended in the affected areas. No disruption to Saudi Aramco’s operations was reported in the information released about the incident.
The latest interception nevertheless highlights the continuing threat to energy infrastructure in a region central to global crude supplies.

title: Bitcoin holds below $76K as Binance EU closures add to crypto market pressure
full_text:
Investing.com -- Bitcoin traded below $76,000 on Sunday as fresh regulatory and security concerns weighed on the cryptocurrency industry, with Binance preparing to close certain European customer accounts and authorities intensifying scrutiny of digital asset transactions.
The world’s largest cryptocurrency was down 0.34% to $75,776.7 at 01:06 ET (06:06 GMT), virtually unchanged on the day, after a difficult week for digital assets. Bitcoin remained below the $80,000 mark as investors assessed regulatory developments and risks surrounding major cryptocurrency platforms.
Binance confirmed plans to close affected European accounts by December 31 following the expiration of the European Union’s Markets in Crypto-Assets transition period.
Customers in France, Spain, Italy and Poland have reported receiving withdrawal notices. Deposits have been blocked for affected accounts, although withdrawals remain available.
From November 29, Binance plans to charge remaining balances a monthly fee of 0.025%, or 10 USDC, whichever is higher. Another charge is scheduled after December 24.
The restrictions follow Binance’s failure so far to obtain authorization under the EU’s unified licensing framework. The exchange withdrew its Greek license application in June and continues pursuing regulatory approval elsewhere in Europe.
Separately, the EU established a cryptocurrency task force to combat Russian sanctions evasion through digital assets. The 12-month initiative will coordinate enforcement among member states and target networks facilitating prohibited transactions.
Security concerns intensified after crypto debit card provider Gnosis Pay disclosed unauthorized access to its consumer system on November 3.
Exposed information included customer addresses, payment card numbers and linked cryptocurrency wallets, potentially allowing criminals to connect individuals with their digital asset holdings.
Gnosis Pay said customer funds were unaffected and the breach was contained. The company has strengthened fraud monitoring ahead of its legacy consumer system’s planned December shutdown.
Meanwhile, Strategy executive chairman Michael Saylor defended the company’s bitcoin-backed financing approach, highlighting its Stretch preferred shares as a mechanism for raising capital and supporting cryptocurrency holdings.
Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse also reaffirmed XRP’s central role in the company’s strategy, linking its RLUSD stablecoin expansion to greater liquidity and institutional activity.
For Bitcoin investors, the developments add regulatory compliance, exchange accessibility, and customer security to an already challenging market environment, with the cryptocurrency struggling to regain momentum above $80,000.

title: Turkey’s coal dependence faces scrutiny as COP31 climate summit begins
full_text:
Investing.com -- Turkey’s reliance on coal is facing renewed scrutiny ahead of the COP31 climate summit, as communities affected by mining operations urge world leaders to examine the environmental damage linked to the country’s largest electricity source.
The United Nations climate conference begins Monday in Antalya and runs through November 20, with the transition toward cleaner energy among the central issues under discussion.
Residents of Ikizkoy, near the Akbelen forest in southwestern Mugla province, want delegates to visit communities affected by decades of lignite mining and the expansion of nearby coal operations.
Coal generated 34% of Turkey’s electricity last year, making the country Europe’s largest producer of coal-fired power, according to energy research group Ember.
Mining operations around Akbelen supply the Yenikoy and Kemerkoy power plants, which together generate slightly more than 2% of Turkey’s electricity.
The facilities are operated by Yenikoy-Kemerkoy Energy, a joint venture involving Turkish companies Limak and IC Ictas.
Turkey is proposing a voluntary global electrification target at COP31, although its climate benefits would depend on whether additional electricity comes from low-carbon sources.
Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar acknowledged the difficulties of reducing coal dependence, citing thousands of jobs supported by mining operations.
Ankara considers nuclear power a major alternative and aims to develop 10 gigawatts of nuclear generation capacity by 2040, roughly equivalent to the country’s current coal-powered output.
The Akbelen dispute has also raised questions about restrictions on environmental demonstrations.
Local campaigners say mining expansion threatens forests, agricultural land and nearby communities. Protesters have faced arrests, fines and criminal proceedings following demonstrations against land expropriation and tree clearing.
Human Rights Watch reported in October that Turkish authorities had arbitrarily detained and prosecuted environmental protesters, raising concerns about restrictions on peaceful assembly.
Turkish authorities maintain that police intervene when demonstrations violate the law or threaten public order.
The dispute highlights the challenges facing Turkey as it seeks to balance energy security, employment, and climate commitments during its presidency of the global negotiations.

title: What are the AI lab compute commitments?
full_text:
Investing.com -- OpenAI’s artificial intelligence computing commitments could translate into $614 billion of infrastructure spending through 2030, substantially below widely cited figures of $750 billion, according to Bernstein analyst Mark Moerdler, who sees limited immediate risk for major cloud providers.
The estimate assumes every identified contract proceeds on schedule, an outcome considered unlikely as construction delays, cancellations and flexible hardware purchases could reduce or defer payments.
Annual infrastructure spending could peak at $184 billion in 2031, with costs increasing gradually as data centers become operational rather than arriving as immediate liabilities.
The distinction matters for investors concerned that AI developers have promised more computing capacity than their revenues can support. Some announced partnerships lack fixed delivery schedules or binding purchase quantities, making headline commitments an unreliable measure of near-term cash requirements.
OpenAI reportedly reached nearly $50 billion in annualized revenue in September, with revenue growing 77% year over year. Sustained growth could help fund the expanding infrastructure requirements, although projections remain uncertain.
Oracle’s relationship centers on approximately $300 billion in contracted capacity, delivered in stages under agreements lasting five to six years. OpenAI accounts for less than half of Oracle’s remaining performance obligations, limiting concentration relative to some investor fears.
Microsoft has a separate $250 billion Azure services commitment from OpenAI, with computing capacity supplied in six-year tranches. Its diversified cloud operations could cushion delays better than smaller infrastructure specialists.
Amazon has agreements totaling $138 billion across seven- and eight-year terms, including capacity involving its Trainium processors.
CoreWeave’s OpenAI agreements total up to $22.4 billion, but those figures represent contract ceilings rather than guaranteed revenue. Renewal prospects remain less certain as competing capacity becomes available.
The bigger industry risk may emerge when computing shortages ease, exposing speculative construction projects and providers dependent on expensive financing. Existing contracts with established cloud companies appear more resilient than future demand for specialized computing rentals.

title: China energy investment to hit $940 billion in 2026 as grid spending rises
full_text:
Investing.com -- China’s energy investment is projected to reach $940 billion in 2026, the highest of any country, as the world’s second-largest economy shifts spending toward electricity grids and infrastructure needed to support its expanding renewable energy sector.
The forecast comes from the Global Energy Transition Report 2026, released by the China Enterprise Reform and Development Society and reported by state broadcaster CCTV on Sunday.
China’s renewable energy expansion has created growing demand for transmission networks and supporting infrastructure capable of handling electricity generated from wind, solar and other renewable sources.
The International Energy Agency expects Chinese investment in power grids to reach approximately $140 billion this year, reflecting a shift from building generation capacity toward integrating existing and newly installed facilities.
At the end of 2025, China’s installed renewable power capacity reached 2.337 billion kilowatts, representing 60.1% of the country’s total installed electricity generation capacity.
The country also accounted for 63.6% of newly installed renewable capacity worldwide, highlighting its dominant position in global renewable energy development.
Renewable electricity generation totaled 3.99 trillion kilowatt-hours, equivalent to 38.3% of China’s electricity output. Growth in renewable generation was sufficient to cover the entire increase in national electricity consumption.
The expansion has also reduced coal’s contribution to the country’s power supply. Coal-fired generation accounted for 49.7% of electricity output in the first half of 2026, falling below 50% for the first time.
China’s energy-related carbon dioxide emissions declined 0.5% in 2025, according to the report, reflecting changes in the country’s electricity generation mix.
The country remains a major supplier of renewable energy equipment, producing approximately 70% of the world’s wind-power equipment and 80% of photovoltaic equipment.
Its increasing focus on grid development could support demand for electrical equipment, transmission technology, and energy infrastructure as renewable capacity continues expanding.

title: How Mercedes suffered a €14bn EBIT drop
full_text:
Investing.com -- Mercedes-Benz Cars has suffered a €14 billion decline in annual operating profit from its 2022 peak to estimated 2026 levels, with weakness outside China accounting for at least half the damage, according to Citi analysts.
The bank said investors may be placing too much emphasis on China, where falling sales and shrinking joint venture earnings have dominated concerns about the German automaker’s performance.
Citi estimates China’s total contribution to Mercedes-Benz Cars earnings before interest and taxes historically ranged from €4 billion to €8 billion, falling to slightly above €2 billion in 2026. Its calculations include local joint venture profits, imported vehicle margins, parts sales and royalties.
On those assumptions, Chinese operations could contribute more EBIT this year than the division reports overall, implying that profits from operations outside China have virtually disappeared.
Citi stated that non-China EBIT has fallen from a peak near €8 billion to almost zero, despite sales outside China remaining around 1.4 million vehicles annually since 2021. That compares with approximately 1.8 million before the pandemic and the company’s shift toward luxury models.
A reversal in vehicle pricing is one major factor. Average selling prices have declined from €77,000 in 2024 to an estimated €67,000 in 2026, reducing revenue by roughly €10 billion.
A drop of more than 100,000 vehicles in direct imports to China has removed another estimated €10 billion in revenue. Lower Chinese joint venture production also reduces demand for European-made components, weakening cost absorption at factories outside China.
Other pressures include more than €2 billion annually in U.S. tariffs on European imports, higher electric vehicle penetration, depreciation and broader cost inflation.
Citi sees little prospect of a rebound in Chinese demand, pricing or tariff relief. It argues Mercedes must instead resize production capacity and expenses to match lower revenue, a restructuring process likely to take time.
The bank maintained its Neutral stance and said similar profitability challenges affect BMW and Volkswagen.

title: Turkish villagers demand COP31 leaders see for themselves devastation caused by coal
full_text:
By Ali Kucukgocmen
IKIZKOY, Turkey, Nov 8 (Reuters) - Local official Nejla Isik is among the villagers living beside a coal mine who demand that world leaders gathering in Turkey for COP31 climate talks leave the conference venue to inspect the devastation decades of lignite extraction have caused.
Beginning on Monday, the transition to cleaner energy will be among the themes at the UN conference that continues until November 20 in Antalya on Turkey’s Mediterranean coast.
Isik, an elected official for her community, says the government leaders and UN officials need to head a few hundred kilometres west to Ikizkoy, near the Akbelen forest in Turkey’s southwestern Mugla province, and see for themselves the impact of coal on nature and on people’s lives.
Villagers, who for years have protested against coal mining, have been fined and arrested.
"They should come here, those heads of state. They should come not to Antalya but to Akbelen, to Ikizkoy," said Isik. Her home in Ikizkoy is only a few hundred metres behind a lignite mine that has crept nearer over decades of expansion. Lignite is the lowest grade of coal, meaning burning it releases higher amounts of carbon dioxide than more energy-dense coal.
ELECTRIFICATION, BUT WILL IT BE GREEN?
So far one of the prominent aims of COP31 is to agree a voluntary goal on increasing electrification, proposed by host country Turkey, but unless the electricity is low-carbon it will not curb planet-warming emissions.
Last year, coal was Turkey’s largest electricity source, generating 34% of the country’s power, making Turkey Europe’s biggest coal-fired electricity generator, according to energy think tank Ember. The mines in the Akbelen area provide coal for plants that generate just over 2% of Turkey’s power, according to the operator’s website.
Villagers and environmental campaigners like Isik, who oppose the expansion of lignite mining, say it has destroyed forest and threatens olive groves, farmland and communities.
The fight against coal has had harsh consequences. Isik’s 26-year-old daughter Esra spent 42 days in pretrial detention after a protest against the planned expropriation of land for mining. A court in July sentenced her to two years in prison for resisting public officials. She is free pending the decision of an appeal.
"This punishment was not just handed to me. It was an attempt to punish everyone in this country who stands up for their rights, their land and their village," Esra Isik said.
Her mother has for years protested against the expansion of coal mining around her village.
“For 40 years we’ve been living with coal breathing down our necks. I try to live here with the breath of coal, with the dirt of coal,” Nejla Isik said.
The coal supplies the nearby Yenikoy and Kemerkoy power plants, operated by Yenikoy-Kemerkoy Energy, a joint venture involving Limak and IC Ictas.
Limak declined to comment for this story. IC Ictas did not respond to a request for comment.
At a meeting with foreign media on Thursday, Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar said Turkey was working on a just transition to cleaner energy, but that it was difficult as the mines employ thousands of people.
He said nuclear energy offered the most viable alternative and Ankara was aiming for 10 gigawatts of nuclear generation capacity by 2040. That would equate roughly to current coal-powered production, according to Reuters calculations.
RESTRICTIONS ON PROTESTS IN TURKEY
Rights groups have raised concerns about restrictions on protests in Turkey, including blanket bans on demonstrations, mass detentions and what they say is the disproportionate use of force.
Human Rights Watch said in an October report that Turkish authorities had arbitrarily arrested and prosecuted environmental protesters in Akbelen and other parts of the country. It said security forces forcibly dispersed non-violent demonstrations and protesters, lawyers and journalists faced charges such as illegal assembly, obstructing public officials, trespass and spreading false information.
“With Turkey about to host the annual UN climate change summit, its environmental crackdown is a salient reminder of its intolerance of dissent,” said Deniz Bayram, assistant Europe and Central Asia researcher at Human Rights Watch.
The government says police intervene when demonstrations are unlawful or threaten public order. The interior ministry and justice ministry did not comment for this story.
The dispute around Akbelen intensified in 2023 when tree-felling resumed. Villagers say security forces used water cannon and pepper spray on demonstrators seeking to enter the forest and that other punishments followed.
“We were subjected to water cannon, pepper gas, detention, everything,” Nejla Isik said. “Afterwards, because we didn’t abandon this area, this village, there were fines, and a year later cases were opened against us.”
Hasan Yorulmaz, another resident, said protesters had marched to stop pine trees being cut down when soldiers blocked their path.
“They used pepper spray on women and men, young and old,” he said. “Despite that, we continued the resistance. I was at the front and they took me away and detained me.”

title: Stockland drops Sydney data center plans after community opposition
full_text:
Investing.com -- Australian property developer Stockland has abandoned plans to include a data center in a major Sydney logistics development following opposition from local residents, highlighting growing resistance to infrastructure supporting artificial intelligence.
The company confirmed that its proposed development on a former golf course near Sydney Airport would proceed without a data center in the next planning stage.
The nearly two-square-kilometer project, being developed in partnership with John Boyd Properties, occupies land alongside the Cooks River, close to Sydney Airport and Port Botany.
Initially announced in 2025, the development attracted criticism after Stockland introduced data centers as a possible alternative use earlier this year.
The developer had previously identified the site’s proximity to major transport infrastructure as an advantage for a logistics precinct incorporating other commercial activities, including retail and hospitality.
Stockland said it would continue discussions with stakeholders as planning for the broader project progresses. The decision removes the data center component but does not amount to cancellation of the entire logistics development.
The reversal comes as Australian communities increasingly question the electricity and water requirements of large data centers, particularly as technology companies expand computing infrastructure to support AI applications.
Similar concerns have disrupted other projects across the country, creating additional uncertainty for developers seeking suitable locations and reliable electricity connections.
In October, Australian data center operator NEXTDC placed development plans on hold after public opposition delayed power supply to a major project in Melbourne.
The delays also prompted NEXTDC to reduce its outlook, illustrating how infrastructure constraints and community objections can affect project schedules and business expectations.
Another Australian developer, Firmus Grid, encountered opposition to its proposed data center developments. The company subsequently shelved a planned stock market listing after failing to attract sufficient investor support for its proposed $30 billion valuation.
For developers, the setbacks point to growing challenges in securing community acceptance and the infrastructure needed for large computing facilities, potentially complicating Australia’s efforts to accommodate rising demand for AI processing capacity.

title: South Africa’s ANC battered by local election losses ahead of coalition talks
full_text:
By Nellie Peyton
JOHANNESBURG, Nov 8 (Reuters) - South Africa’s African National Congress (ANC) was dealt a stinging blow in last week’s municipal elections, near-complete results showed on Sunday, weakening its hand in the coalition talks that will follow to form city governments.
With 99% of votes counted, the ANC had 31% against 25% for its main rival, the Democratic Alliance (DA). Former President Jacob Zuma’s party uMkhonto weSizwe had about 10% of votes, putting it in third place, while the rest was split between hundreds of smaller parties.
Final results are expected to be announced at 6 p.m. (1600 GMT).
The outcome marks a painful setback for the ANC, which has seen its vote share fall steadily in local elections over the last 15 years due largely to failures in basic services such as water and electricity.
Since no party won more than 50% of votes in many cities including South Africa’s commercial hub Johannesburg, the ANC and DA will have to team up, or hash it out with smaller parties to form majority municipal governments.
COALITION TALKS TO START SOON
ANC Secretary-General Fikile Mbalula called the result "catastrophic" for the ANC but said the party would not go begging for positions when coalition talks begin soon.
"When the people tell us we have fallen short... the honest answer is not to argue with them but to go home and put our house in order," Mbalula said on Saturday.
Parties will have 14 days to negotiate before city councils are formed.
In Johannesburg, the pro-business DA led the count with about 35% of votes, compared to 20% for the ANC.
That could give DA veteran Helen Zille, who had campaigned on fixing potholes and leaking water pipes, a good chance of becoming mayor, depending on the coalition agreements reached.
The DA said in a statement that it would initiate coalition discussions with "political parties that share a commitment to clean and accountable government, rooting out corruption, service delivery for all, the rule of law, and non-racialism".

title: Who is Qiulae Wong, the outsider who could decide New Zealand’s next government?
full_text:
By Alasdair Pal
WELLINGTON, Nov 8 (Reuters) - Qiulae Wong has been a politician for less than a year, but the 38-year-old could hold the balance of power in New Zealand’s parliament after initial counting in Saturday’s general election ended without a clear victor.
Prime Minister Christopher Luxon’s centre-right coalition could govern with a majority of just two seats, Electoral Commission preliminary results showed, but that slim margin could disappear once special votes, which typically favour the left, are released at the official count on November 27.
That would mean either a centre-right or centre-left bloc would require the support of Wong’s centrist Opportunity Party, which looks likely to enter parliament for the first time. Either Luxon’s National party or Labour, led by Chris Hipkins, are expected to try to form a coalition government in the coming days or weeks.
Wong, a former sustainable-business consultant, answered a job advertisement to head the decade-old party, taking over in November 2025.
She quickly oversaw a rebrand and dramatic rise in Opportunity’s popularity, and its current vote share of 5.96% would give it seven seats in a 131-member parliament, Electoral Commission data showed.
"It might seem like we’ve just arrived, that this is an overnight success, but to many in this room, this result has been a long time coming," Wong told cheering supporters in Auckland on Saturday night.
SWEEPING TAX PROPOSALS
Opportunity’s flagship policies centre on tax, with an annual NZ$19,400 ($10,800) universal basic income for most New Zealand residents funded by a 1.75% annual land tax. The party also wants to simplify the country’s income tax system.
“There’s also been a shift globally around seeing the need to tax work less and tax wealth more or tax assets more. And so that’s what this tax reset package is designed to do: take some of the burden off income tax and place that onto property,” Wong told Reuters in an interview in August.
A basic income for residents would be a first for a developed economy. Dozens of countries have land taxes, but they usually exclude primary residences, unlike Opportunity’s proposal.
National and Labour have both ruled out adopting Opportunity’s tax policies, while Luxon has said dozens of times during campaigning he would not enter into coalition with Opportunity.
Wong has said she would look to negotiate with the party that secures the largest number of seats in parliament and that it would be possible to find common ground with National or Labour.
"There are different forms of us working with other parties, whether that’s coalition, confidence and supply, being on the crossbenches, and all of those options are on the table for us right now," she told public broadcaster TVNZ on Saturday.
"We have to we have to look at how the votes land."

title: Poland in shock after six die in Krakow mass shooting
full_text:
By Jakub Porzycki, Karol Badohal and Marek Strzelecki
KRAKOW, Nov 7 (Reuters) - A Polish gunman likely influenced by far-right ideology killed six people in the main square of the southern city of Krakow before police shot and arrested him, officials said on Saturday, adding that three more bodies were found in his home.
The scenes of blood and bodies strewn across the historic heart of one of Poland’s main tourist attractions shocked a nation that has long viewed itself as safer than western European neighbours that have witnessed such attacks in the past.
The mass shooting of unprecedented scale adds to the sense of unease built by a string of school stabbings in October which authorities said was influenced by violent and extremist content online.
"Everything points to the fact that the shooter was influenced by far-right ideology, a matter that will also be subject to investigation," Interior Minister Marcin Kierwinski told a news briefing.
"Police officers are on-site, as are agents from the Internal Security Agency, both here at the scene and at the individual’s family home."
Polish authorities have said four women and two men were killed in the attack in the city centre. Seventeen others, including two police officers and the assailant, were wounded.
Police said one of the dead people identified so far was a British citizen.
An interior ministry spokesperson said that the five foreign nationals injured in the shooting came from Austria, Germany, Portugal, Russia and Britain.
A spokesperson for the Lesser Poland Voivodeship office, the southern region where Krakow lies, told Reuters shortly after midnight local time that the injured police officers were in stable condition after undergoing surgery, and the justice minister called for blood donations for one of the wounded officers.
The spokesman also said the shooter was in "stable but very critical condition" after multiple surgeries. Videos posted online had shown the assailant falling to the ground during a close-range shootout with police officers firing handguns.
BODIES FOUND AT GUNMAN’S HOUSE
Prime Minister Donald Tusk said that the bodies of two women and one man had been found at the shooter’s home in Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski, just under 200 kilometres north of Krakow.
"There are strong indications that they are members of his immediate family," Tusk told a crisis meeting.
He said a drone had been used to look inside the gunman’s home due to potential security threats.
"We know that a significant amount of weaponry may be inside the house," he said.
Local media in Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski reported that residents had been evacuated from the building where the gunman lived and that counterterrorism officers had entered the building.
Speaking along with the prime minister, Tomasz Siemoniak, the minister coordinating special services, said Poland’s Internal Security Agency (ABW) and Military Counterintelligence Service (SKW) are supporting the investigation.
MILITARY-STYLE CLOTHES
Katarzyna Cislo, a local police spokesperson, said: "The shooter was wearing military-like clothes and used military weapons. Many ... weapons and ammunition were found in his vehicle too."
Police spokesperson Andrzej Fijolek told private broadcaster TVN 24 that the assailant used an AR-15 rifle and that he had a firearms licence.
According to police, the alleged gunman was a 24-year-old Polish citizen. "The only known perpetrator of the incident is in police custody," they added in a post on X. They did not mention a motive for the shootings.
Police said they started to receive reports at around 3 p.m. (1400 GMT) that an assailant had opened fire from a car and had shot randomly at people in the square in Poland’s second-largest city, a popular tourist destination.
Unverified footage shared on social media showed people fleeing the scene as shots rang out and police sirens blared. Other video showed two people lying on blood-spattered paving stones and bystanders trying to resuscitate them. A third person lay motionless on the ground nearby.
"I saw shots being fired from the driver’s side window, and smoke was coming out. I ran to the police station in the main market square; when I burst inside, it was full of people hiding on the floor," a man who gave his name only as Konrad, and witnessed the shooting, told news website Interia.
A 67-year-old man called Julek told Reuters that he saw a dark car appear suddenly before the driver started shooting at a group of people and drove off.
"If we had been two minutes earlier, we might have been shot," he said.
Unverified footage on social media showed shooting in the Main Market Square as traditional horse-drawn carriages, popular with tourists, passed through or were parked nearby.
A man could be seen taking cover in one of the many restaurants and cafes that line the elegant square.
NATIONAL MOURNING
Kierwinski praised the heroism of officers who apprehended the suspect.
"The police prevented a much larger massacre that could have otherwise occurred," he said. "They fired shots at the attacker just three minutes after receiving the report."
A spokesperson for President Karol Nawrocki said he would declare a period of national mourning on November 8 and 9.
"My thoughts are with the victims, those injured, and their families," Nawrocki wrote on X.
Expressions of shock and condolence flooded in from around Europe.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy called the shooting "shocking." "On behalf of the Ukrainian people, and personally, I extend my sincere condolences to the families and loved ones of the victims," he wrote on X.
European foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas called it "a tragedy that will be felt far beyond Poland."

title: Pope Leo urges South America to bridge divides on Uruguay stop of 12-day tour
full_text:
By Joshua McElwee and Lucinda Elliott
MONTEVIDEO, Nov 7 (Reuters) - Pope Leo on Saturday urged an estimated 40,000 people, many of whom waited overnight in the rain on the Uruguay-Argentina border for his visit, to bridge their differences as he toured a region marked by sharp political divisions.
Leo, on an ambitious 12-day, three-country tour through November 17, travelled some 750 km (466 miles) back and forth from Montevideo to Paysandu, a riverside economic hub in Uruguay’s northwest, where crowds gathered in heavy rain that eased shortly before his arrival.
He was the first pope to visit the city on the Uruguay River, chosen by the Vatican as the location for Leo’s first Mass in South America because it is accessible to pilgrims across the region.
The crowd in a sprawling park on the southern edge of the city erupted into cheers and blew loud horns as Leo toured in an open-top popemobile amid blustery winds.
In his sermon, Leo drew inspiration from the nearby General Artigas International Bridge, which connects Uruguay and Argentina.
"It is not difficult to imagine the benefits a bridge brings: openness, communication and exchange. That is why it is so important to be builders of bridges!" he said.
"This is the vocation to which we are all called: to build bridges, strengthen bonds, unite, communicate."
After returning to Montevideo for an evening vigil at Centenary Stadium, a soccer venue better known for sporting events than religious gatherings, Leo was greeted by a crowd estimated by the Vatican at about 100,000 people chanting, "Pope Leo, we love you so much."
Mathias Franco, 18, who was there with two friends, said the turnout was striking in a country known for its strong secular tradition. A survey in Uruguay by polling firm Cifra found just a third of adults identify as Catholic — exceptionally low for Latin America — while another 28% believe in God but do not feel affiliated with any religion.
"We’re always told this is the most secular country in Latin America, but events like this show something different," he said. "I see this visit as a big opportunity for Uruguay, for us to grow as a community."
Inside the stadium, folk music greeted pilgrims as they streamed in, creating an atmosphere that felt more like a concert than a prayer vigil.
POPE URGES REGIONAL COOPERATION
The 71-year-old pontiff is making one of the most demanding foreign trips by a Catholic leader in decades less than a month after undergoing lung cancer surgery.
Leo, the first US-born pope, is visiting Uruguay, one of Latin America’s more stable democracies, until Sunday on the first stop of a tour that will also take him to Argentina and Peru.
The Vatican has described the trip as a "homecoming" for Leo, who served as a missionary in Peru for decades and became a Peruvian citizen.
The pope, who has forcefully decried the direction of global leadership in recent months, is expected to address a range of issues facing the continent on the tour, including environmental destruction, arms trafficking and regional political instability.
POPE VISITS TROUBLED MONTEVIDEO NEIGHBORHOOD
Leo on Saturday afternoon made a visit to Casavalle, a neighborhood on the northern outskirts of Montevideo scarred by violence and drug-related crime.
The pope walked among makeshift houses with corrugated metal roofing and unfinished construction projects then listened to local residents, including a mother who cried as she recounted raising a child while homeless.
Leo gave the woman a hug and in his own remarks urged Uruguayans to "shake off" apathy towards poverty and inequality and help those in need. "We cannot ignore the many people around us who are suffering," he said.
Pablo Coimbra, pastor of a church near where Leo visited, told Reuters before the pope’s arrival that he hoped Leo would lift the spirits of a community that often feels overlooked.
"It is an area forgotten by governments and institutions," Coimbra said of the neighborhood, classified as a police "red" zone, where residents often hear gunfire amid territorial disputes between drug dealers.
The pope wraps up his Uruguay visit on Sunday morning. On Sunday afternoon he heads to Argentina, where he will give a speech to President Javier Milei, a libertarian seen as a close ally of US President Donald Trump, who lambasted Leo earlier this year after the pope criticized the Iran war.
